activity: DE testing & Controls handover to SOM
description: DE Testing = Design Effectiveness Testing. It validates whether a control is designed correctly to mitigate the intended risk before the control becomes operational. All SOX controls require mandatory DE testing before handover to SOM. Non‑SOX controls may or may not require DE testing, depending on risk-based selection (e.g., high‑criticality RMF controls). Lack of DE testing before handover might led to controls failing IRM testing, causing rework and heavy remediation effort in operations. Post DE testing is successful, explicit KT to be provided to SOM team (+ supplier if controls execution is outsourced to a supplier) on controls and execution steps as part of handover.
action_owner: Project (provide details & ERS (review/accessment) team

activity: Regression testing, Functional testing, Performance testing and Integration testing and evaluation of results (particularly for critical CVPs)

SOM relies on these test phases to confirm stability, protect existing functionality, validate end‑to‑end flows, and ensure the system performs predictably under real‑world loads. Evaluation of results—especially for critical CVPs—helps SOM identify risks early, ensure defect‑free handover, and secure operational readiness. We should have test strategy defined along with delivery team particularly to understand what will be the level of test scripts identified for the following: - unit testing - integrated testing - performance testing - functional testing - regression testing

activity: Mitigation actions for any issues found in Regression testing, Functional testing, Performance testing and Integration testing

Particularly for performance testing, it is important to benchmark performance metrics (speed, runtime, latency etc) for critical product journey touchpoints.
